second-law.def: Newton's second law: the acceleration of an object (or of a system's center of mass) equals the net external force divided by the mass, a = ΣF/m, and points in the direction of the net force.

system-acceleration.def: The acceleration of a system's center of mass, a_sys = ΣF_ext / m_sys: the net external force divided by the total mass. Internal forces do not enter.

connected-objects.def: Objects joined by ideal strings or pushing on each other so that they share one acceleration, such as a cart pulled by a hanging block or an Atwood machine (two masses hung over one pulley).
